title: Chevrolet Impala Engines by Year (1958–2020)
description: Every factory engine in the Chevrolet Impala by year, 1958–2020: the 348 and 409, 327, 396, 427 and 454 V8s, the LT1 Impala SS, and the front-drive V6s.
intro: The Impala began in 1958 as the top Bel Air and became Chevrolet's best-selling full-size car. It was built through 1985, revived as the rear-drive Impala SS for 1994–1996, and returned as a front-drive sedan from 2000 to 2020.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The early Impala offered the 348 W-series V8 and, from 1961, the 409. The 1963 Z11 427 was a factory drag-racing package.
Big blocks took over from the 409 during 1965: the 396 and, from 1966, the 427.
Ratings are SAE net from 1972. The 454 stayed available through 1976.
The downsized 1977 Impala ran from the 250 six to the 350, with V6s and an Oldsmobile-built 5.7 diesel in the early 1980s, and Chevrolet's 4.3 V6 for 1985.

generations.name: Impala SS
intro: The Impala SS used the 5.7 LT1 V8, rated at 260 hp, in the Caprice body.
The front-drive Impala used GM's 60-degree V6s, a supercharged 3800 in the 2004–2005 SS, a 5.3 V8 in the 2006–2009 SS, and from 2012 the 3.6 V6, with a 2.5 four from 2014.
